title: Etale open tensor and coefficient comparisons with counit normalization
statement:
Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion of schemes, let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, and use constant ring sheaves on small etale sites and their ordinary unbounded module derived categories. Write $j_!$ for exact extension by zero, $j^*$ for exact restriction, and $F_T=-\otimes_A^L B$ on $T=U,X$. For all $P\in D(U_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $T\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ the canonical map
$$\gamma_{P,T}:j_!(P\otimes_A^L j^*T)\longrightarrow j_!P\otimes_A^L T$$
is an isomorphism. It is the $j_!\dashv j^*$-adjunct of the identity under $j^*j_!\cong1$ and the restriction/tensor comparison. On module sheaves the same formula holds for ordinary tensor. Extension by zero preserves flat module sheaves and K-flat complexes. There is a natural $B$-linear isomorphism $q_{j,P}:F_Xj_!P\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!F_UP$ whose restriction to $U$ is the identity under the canonical tensor identifications. Under $F_Uj^*\cong j^*F_X$ it satisfies
$$\epsilon_{j,B,F_XT}\circ j_!(F_Uj^*T\cong j^*F_XT)\circ q_{j,j^*T}=F_X(\epsilon_{j,A,T}).$$
The tensor and scalar comparisons commute with associativity and successive scalar extension under their canonical identifications. All comparisons and the derived adjunction are normalized by degreewise extension of the open sheaf adjunction; no boundedness or constructibility assumption is made.

Notation and categorical conventions are those of [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero], [def-kun-derived-tensor], [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], [def-pc-kflat-complex], [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction].

proof.text: Regard $U$ as an object of $X_{\mathrm{et}}$: an open immersion is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]. The equivalence $X_{\mathrm{et}}/U\simeq U_{\mathrm{et}}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-site-localization-open] keeps the underlying test schemes, their section rings and coverings. It therefore also identifies constant-ring module sheaves, their restriction, and the direct-sum extension presheaves in [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. Thus [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] applies with $\mathcal O=A_X$, and also with $B_X$: $j_!,j^*$ are exact and $j_!\dashv j^*$. We use the specific Hom bijection and the counit formula of [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction], not an unspecified adjunction.

source.place: Tags 03DH (localized ringed site), 03DJ (exactness); etale-cohomology.tex Tag 0F70 (open case)

proof.text: The open unit $P\to j^*j_!P$ is an isomorphism on abelian sheaves by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-unit-iso]. The module constructions have the same underlying abelian sheaves: module sheafification is the abelian sheafification with its unique extending action [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. The unit is linear, and the inverse of an invertible linear map is linear, so the unit is also an isomorphism for $A$- and $B$-module sheaves. Its normalization is the identity on a section over a test scheme factoring through $U$, by the Hom formula in [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction]. In particular, for maps with source $j_!P$, restriction followed by the open unit is precisely the adjunction bijection; it detects equality of maps. Between objects in the image of $j_!$, restriction also detects isomorphisms: use this bijection to lift the inverse of a restricted map, and its injectivity to check the inverse laws.

For module sheaves $P,T$, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor] gives a natural isomorphism between $j_!(P\otimes_A j^*T)$ and $j_!P\otimes_A T$. Define $\gamma^0$ to be the adjunct of the unit at $P$ tensored with $j^*T$, followed by the inverse of the restriction/tensor isomorphism. That restriction/tensor isomorphism, including its pure-tensor normalization, is [lem-sfb-localized-site-tensor-restriction]. Under the unit identifications, $j^*\gamma^0$ is the identity. Both endpoints are in the essential image of $j_!$ by the cited slice tensor identity. Step 2 therefore proves that this particular $\gamma^0$ is invertible, rather than merely that its endpoints are isomorphic. The construction is natural. On a test scheme factoring through $U$ its local pure-tensor formula is $j_!(p\otimes t)\mapsto j_!(p)\otimes t$; this follows directly from its adjunct and the specified restriction comparison.

Let $P$ be a flat $A_U$-module sheaf, and tensor a short exact sequence of $A_X$-modules with $j_!P$. Step 3 identifies the resulting sequence with $j_!$ of its restriction tensored with $P$. Restriction and extension by zero are exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], and the middle tensor functor is exact by flatness [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. The result is exact. This is exactly flatness of $j_!P$; no stalk or finite-ring criterion is being used.

An exact additive functor commutes with cohomology, since it preserves the kernels, images and cokernels defining it; thus both open functors preserve acyclic complexes and quasi-isomorphisms. As a left adjoint, $j_!$ preserves direct sums. Applying step 3 to every bidegree therefore gives an isomorphism of direct-sum total complexes
$$j_!K\otimes_A C\cong j_!(K\otimes_A j^*C).$$
It commutes with the two differential terms $d_K\otimes1$ and $(-1)^p1\otimes d_C$ by naturality [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. If $K$ is K-flat and $C$ is acyclic, the right side is acyclic, proving that $j_!K$ is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex]. We will also need restriction of K-flat complexes: for K-flat $R$ on $X$ and acyclic $C$ on $U$, the same identity makes $j_!(C\otimes_A j^*R)\cong j_!C\otimes_A R$ acyclic. Applying exact $j^*$ and $j^*j_!\cong1$ proves that $C\otimes_A j^*R$ is acyclic. Hence $j^*R$ is K-flat too.

source.place: Tag 0GL1 (lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor), total-complex argument; sites-modules.tex Tags 03DJ and 0E8I

proof.text: The sheaf adjunction induces the termwise adjunction on complexes and homotopy categories with termwise unit and counit by [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy]. By step 5 both functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms. Consequently these functors and natural transformations descend along the derived-category localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; the triangle identities descend as equalities, giving the unbounded adjunction with the required degreewise normalization. The open unit is still invertible, so the equality and isomorphism tests of step 2 apply in the derived categories as well.

source.place: Tag 08FJ (lemma-adjoint-lower-shriek-restrict), exact termwise adjunction localized at quasi-isomorphisms

proof.text: For arbitrary derived $P,T$, choose a K-flat resolution $R\to P$ with flat terms [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], and any complex $C$ representing $T$. By step 5, $j_!R$ is K-flat and $j_!$ preserves the resolution quasi-isomorphism. The definition [def-kun-derived-tensor] thus computes the two sides as $j_!(R\otimes_A j^*C)$ and $j_!R\otimes_A C$. The total-complex isomorphism of step 5 gives $\gamma$. It is the adjunct of the identity because degreewise it is the step-3 adjunct, and step 6 descends that same unit and counit. The K-flat model comparisons and their uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] make the construction natural and independent of resolutions. This proves the claimed derived projection formula on all unbounded objects.

For a module $P$ on $U$ specialize $(\gamma^0)^{-1}$ to $T=B_X$. It is $B_X$-linear: its formula on local tensor generators is $j_!(p)\otimes b\mapsto j_!(p\otimes b)$, which commutes with multiplication by every locally constant section of $B_X$. The same formula and uniqueness of the sheafified action [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] identify the output with the $B$-module extension $j_{!,B}(P\otimes_A B_U)$. Apply this degreewise to a K-flat flat-term resolution $R\to P$. Both $R$ and $j_!R$ are K-flat, so [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] computes $F_UP$ and $F_Xj_!P$ by $R\otimes_A B_U$ and $j_!R\otimes_A B_X$. The resulting isomorphism is $q_{j,P}$ in $D(X_{\mathrm{et}},B)$. It is natural and independent of the resolution by the canonical comparisons in that node. Its restriction is the identity, by the explicit generator formula and the open units.

source.place: Tag 0E8I (tensor identity), specialized to the ring map A_X to B_X; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 06YY (derived change of rings)

proof.text: To specify $r_T:F_Uj^*T\cong j^*F_XT$, choose a K-flat flat-term resolution $R\to T$ on $X$. Step 5 makes $j^*R$ K-flat. The restriction/tensor comparison [lem-sfb-localized-site-tensor-restriction] identifies $(R\otimes_A B_X)|_U$ with $(R|_U)\otimes_A B_U$, with identity pure-tensor formula. Together with [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] this defines $r_T$ canonically; it also shows that restriction of $q$ is the identity for the same identifications, without assuming that $B$ is flat over $A$.

source.place: Tag 06YY (derived change of rings), with sites-modules.tex Tag 03EL (restriction/tensor)

proof.text: Check the counit equation on the K-flat flat-term model $R\to T$ of step 9. The counit $\epsilon_{j,A,R}:j_!j^*R\to R$ is termwise the section map of [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction]. By steps 4--5 its source is also K-flat, so [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] computes $F_X(\epsilon_{j,A,T})$ by this actual chain map tensored with $B$. On an extension-presheaf summand over a test scheme factoring through $U$, the left-hand composite sends $s\otimes b$, successively, to $s\otimes b$ through $q$, to $s\otimes b$ through $r$, and then to the same section $s\otimes b$ by the $B$-counit. The right-hand map does the same. A test scheme not factoring through $U$ has zero extension-presheaf value. Tensor maps are determined locally by these generators, and the sheafification universal property makes the two chain maps equal [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Localization gives exactly the displayed counit equation, with the normalized counits of step 6.

source.place: Tag 03DI (extension adjunction, summand formula), Tag 03CY (module sheafification), Tag 0E8I; derived on K-flat models

proof.text: For the tensor associativity square, choose K-flat flat-term models $R,S,V$ for $P,T_1,T_2$. Restriction keeps K-flatness by step 5 and keeps flat terms by [lem-weil-pbc-slice-restriction-flat]. Rebracketing total tensors sends $((r\otimes s)\otimes v)$ to $r\otimes(s\otimes v)$ and is a chain isomorphism: the three differential terms have signs $1,(-1)^p,(-1)^{p+q}$ in both bracketings [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. A tensor of two K-flat complexes is K-flat, since tensoring an acyclic complex with the first and then the second stays acyclic; the displayed rebracketing identifies this with the test for the product. Thus these are valid models for every vertex. Either path in the open tensor square sends the local generator $j_!((r\otimes s)\otimes v)$ to $(j_!r\otimes s)\otimes v$ under rebracketing. The sheafification universal property gives equality, and the canonical model comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] descend it. This proves tensor associativity compatibility, including the square obtained by specializing a factor to a coefficient ring.

source.place: Tag 0GL1, with sites-modules.tex Tags 0E8I and 0E8J; explicit triple-total-tensor calculation

proof.text: For successive scalar extension $A\to B\to C$, take one K-flat flat-term resolution $R$ of $P$ on $U$. The general ringed-topos pullback theorem [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], applied to the identity geometric morphism and the ring maps $A_U\to B_U$ and $A_X\to B_X$, says that $R\otimes_A B$ and $j_!R\otimes_A B$ remain K-flat with flat terms over $B$. Hence the canonical successive-extension identification is represented by $((r\otimes b)\otimes c)\mapsto r\otimes bc$, with inverse $r\otimes c\mapsto(r\otimes1)\otimes c$. Both the direct $q^{A,C}$ and the composite $q^{B,C}\circ F^{B,C}(q^{A,B})$ send $j_!r\otimes c$ to $j_!(r\otimes c)$ under these identifications. The mixed tensor/scalar square is the same explicit calculation: the strong scalar tensor comparison sends $(j_!r\otimes b_1)\otimes_B(s\otimes b_2)$ to $(j_!r\otimes s)\otimes b_1b_2$. Applying the open comparison before or after it gives $j_!((r\otimes j^*s)\otimes b_1b_2)$ in either case, using the same reassociation and no permutation of the graded factors. Equality follows by sheafification, then by the K-flat comparisons [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. This proves the successive-scalar and mixed associativity clauses. Every argument above uses arbitrary complexes and exact open functors, so no boundedness or constructibility hypothesis has entered.
